content: The Dental Technologists Association (DTA) is a professional organization that represents dental technicians in the United Kingdom. History The association was originally established in 1989 as the Dental Technicians Education and Training Advisory Board (DTETAB), with Colin Lee serving as its chairman. In 2002, DTETAB was renamed the Dental Technicians Association. The final name change occurred in 2006, when it became the Dental Technologists Association. In the same year, the former secretary of the Orthodontic Technicians Association was elected as the first president of the DTA. Aims The objectives of the DTA are as follows: To provide an organization that supports the development of the dental technology profession. To encourage and promote education, including continuing professional development (CPD), for dental technicians. To establish connections with other organizations and bodies for the benefit of dental technicians and patients. To advocate the DTA’s views to the government, relevant groups, service providers, and the public. To adopt and share best practices, enabling dental technology to play a broader role in oral healthcare. To act as a forward-thinking organization that advises, develops, and supports individual dental technicians. To support dental technician members by providing benefits and career opportunities. To maintain and develop the professional title and function of dental technicians. To establish and maintain links with other dental technology and Dental Care Professional (DCP) groups as appropriate. To negotiate with relevant groups on behalf of dental technicians. Offices The headquarters of the DTA is located at 4 Pavilion Court, 600 Pavilion Drive, Brackmills Business Park, Northampton, United Kingdom. The Chief Executive of the association is Sue Adams, who oversees the office, administration, and support for sub-committees, and serves as the first point of contact for members. Council The DTA Council serves as the governing body of the association. Some council members are elected, while others are appointed by specialist dental technology groups. The council is composed of: Eight directly elected dental technicians. Five representatives from specialist dental technology groups. Sub-Committees Executive Committee This committee is responsible for maintaining the development of the council’s proposals. The Chief Executive oversees the day-to-day administration of the association. The Executive Committee formally reports to the council during its biannual meetings. Public Relations The Public Relations Committee is tasked with raising awareness about the association and dental technology in general. Stephen Wears is the current chairman of this committee. Membership Services The Membership Services Committee is responsible for developing services for members, such as a legal helpline. Stephen Wears also serves as the chairman of this committee. Health and Safety The Health and Safety Committee provides members with information on current health and safety issues. Education and Training The Education and Training Committee is responsible for improving educational standards to ensure that current qualifications meet the needs of the industry. John Stacey is the current chairman of this committee.
